items.name: Peer Helpers
items.description: Peer Helpers is a select group of Middle School leaders who are recognized by students and faculty for exemplifying excellence, character, and opportunity. Members apply with a teacher recommendation and serve as helpers and role models at events throughout the year, including new student orientation, parents’ night, panel discussions, Red Ribbon Week, My Mind Matters week, and more. It’s a great fit for students who want to lead by example, welcome others, and make a difference in their school community.

items.name: Crew Council
items.description: Crew Council is the Middle School’s student government. Each homeroom’s representatives are selected by their peers to speak for their classmates, help plan school programming, and lead initiatives that make Middle School a better place for everyone. Members build leadership, teamwork, and communication skills while working with faculty to turn student ideas into action. It’s a great fit for students who care about their school community and want a voice in what happens there.

items.name: Black Scholars Coalition
items.description: A safe haven where students celebrate identity, share experiences, and explore Black culture. Students take part in meaningful activities and dialogue that foster diversity, inclusion, and cultural pride. The group meets on Fridays or after school.

items.schedule: Fridays during community time

items.name: Debate Team
items.description: Explore the debate process and compete against other middle schools. Members learn to build arguments, speak persuasively, and think on their feet while representing Woodward. The team meets on Fridays or after school.
items.schedule: Fridays or after school (exact day and time to be confirmed)

items.name: Academic Team
items.description: Join the academic team for challenging competitions in all subjects. A good fit for curious students who enjoy quiz-style questions and working with teammates. The team meets on Fridays or after school.
items.schedule: Fridays or after school (exact day and time to be confirmed)

items.description: A sideline sport open to boys and girls that requires tryouts for a maximum 20-spot roster. The season runs from April through October. More information is on the Middle School Information and Downloads page.
items.schedule: Season runs April through October (practice days and times to be confirmed)

items.name: Cross Country
items.description: Members run a two-mile distance at meets, which are usually held on weekdays with an occasional Saturday meet. This is a no-cut sport for girls and boys, with an emphasis on individual improvement. A strict attendance policy encourages as much practice time as possible during the short season, and an informational meeting is held for students the first week of school.
items.schedule: Fall season (practice days and times to be confirmed). Meets on weekdays with an occasional Saturday

items.name: Football
items.description: Football is a no-cut sport that begins in early August and ends in mid-October, so every interested student can play. All medical forms and physicals must be updated before attending practice. Players build teamwork, fitness, and football skills over the fall season. Details are on the Middle School Information and Downloads page.
items.schedule: Early August through mid-October (practice days and times to be confirmed)

items.name: Softball
items.description: A girls' sport that requires tryouts. Once school begins, practice is Monday through Thursday from 4:00 to 5:30 PM. Rising 7th and 8th grade softball players are highly encouraged to attend the Woodward Softball Camp over the summer (woodward.edu/summer-programs).
items.schedule: Mondays, Tuesdays, Wednesdays, Thursdays, 4:00–5:30 PM (fall season)

items.name: Tennis
items.description: Open to 7th and 8th grade boys and girls, who may try out for the MS team. Tryouts begin in mid-February and the season ends in May. Matches are held during the week and on Saturdays, and practice is Monday through Friday from 4:00 to 5:45 PM.
items.schedule: Mondays, Tuesdays, Wednesdays, Thursdays, Fridays, 4:00–5:45 PM (spring season, mid-February to May)

items.description: A club exclusively for currently enrolled middle school choir students who want to take their singing to the next level. Members prepare a solo, master their scales, and sharpen their sight-reading skills so they can step into auditions with confidence. Whether you are aiming for top scores or simply want to grow as a musician, sessions are supportive and focused.
items.schedule: Thursdays, during the 30-minute community time (clubs rotate each quarter)

items.name: Anime Club
items.description: Join an incredible journey through some of the best animated storytelling ever created! Members watch and talk about anime with classmates who share the interest. Meets during Thursday community time, and students can join a different club each quarter.

items.schedule: Thursdays, during the 30-minute community time (clubs rotate each quarter)

items.schedule: Thursdays, during the 30-minute community time (clubs rotate each quarter)

items.name: Birthday Club
items.description: The club's goal is to recognize the birthdays of all students and teachers throughout the year. Members create signs to decorate lockers for students and doors for teachers, spreading kindness and school spirit. Meets during Thursday community time, and students can join a different club each quarter.
items.schedule: Thursdays, during the 30-minute community time (clubs rotate each quarter)

items.description: On nice club days, students walk for exercise and pleasure. When the weather is cold or rainy, they play board games instead. A relaxed way to get moving, unwind, and chat with friends. Meets during Thursday community time, and students can join a different club each quarter.
items.location: Outdoors on nice days; indoors in bad weather
items.schedule: Thursdays, during the 30-minute community time (clubs rotate each quarter)

items.name: Book Folding Club

items.description: Use letters to create beautiful design and art. Meets during Thursday community time, and students can join a different club each quarter.
items.schedule: Thursdays, during the 30-minute community time (clubs rotate each quarter)

This club is devoted strictly to card games: no boards, no dice, and no spinners, just cards and friends. Meets during Thursday community time, and students can join a different club each quarter.
items.schedule: Thursdays, during the 30-minute community time (clubs rotate each quarter)

items.name: Checkers Club

items.schedule: Thursdays, during the 30-minute community time (clubs rotate each quarter)

items.schedule: Thursdays, during the 30-minute community time (clubs rotate each quarter)

items.description: A club to watch and discuss movies related to space discovery. Members explore how films imagine space exploration while sharing ideas with classmates. Meets during Thursday community time, and students can join a different club each quarter.
items.schedule: Thursdays, during the 30-minute community time (clubs rotate each quarter)

items.description: Color your world and find your happy place. Members spend the time coloring inside and outside the lines with markers, crayons, or even their iPads, to color their cares away. Meets during Thursday community time, and students can join a different club each quarter.
items.schedule: Thursdays, during the 30-minute community time (clubs rotate each quarter)

items.schedule: Thursdays, during the 30-minute community time (clubs rotate each quarter)

items.name: Harry Potter Club
items.description: A magical experience! Members watch the iconic films, dive into discussions about Hogwarts houses, and test their wizarding knowledge with fun trivia games. Whether you are a Gryffindor, Hufflepuff, Ravenclaw, or Slytherin, there is something for every Potterhead. Meets during Thursday community time, and students can join a different club each quarter.
items.schedule: Thursdays, during the 30-minute community time (clubs rotate each quarter)

items.name: Fantasy Football Club

items.schedule: Thursdays, during the 30-minute community time (clubs rotate each quarter)

items.schedule: Thursdays, during the 30-minute community time (clubs rotate each quarter)

items.schedule: Thursdays, during the 30-minute community time (clubs rotate each quarter)

items.schedule: Thursdays, during the 30-minute community time (clubs rotate each quarter)

items.name: Write It Out Club
items.description: A space to come together and work through journaling as a way to reflect through writing. Meets during Thursday community time, and students can join a different club each quarter.
items.schedule: Thursdays, during the 30-minute community time (clubs rotate each quarter)

items.name: Equality Alliance
items.description: EA works toward creating and maintaining a safe, inclusive, and equitable community for LGBTQIA+ students, faculty, and parents. The group aims to sustain visibility and a sense of community throughout the school. The group meets on Fridays or after school.
items.schedule: Fridays or after school (exact day and time to be confirmed)

items.name: Interfaith Club
items.description: A place for students of all faith backgrounds to come together, share about their "uniquely cool" traditions, and learn from one another. The club also helps lead assembly talks on special holidays throughout the year. The group meets on Fridays or after school.
items.schedule: Fridays or after school (exact day and time to be confirmed)

items.name: Math Team
items.description: A team for bright, curious students who want increased brain power through math challenges. The team meets on Fridays or after school.
items.schedule: Fridays or after school (exact day and time to be confirmed)

items.name: Nesher
items.description: A Jewish affinity group that provides a supportive community where Jewish students can connect, share experiences, and celebrate Jewish identity, culture, and traditions. The group meets on Fridays or after school.
items.schedule: Fridays or after school (exact day and time to be confirmed)

items.name: Robotics Team
items.description: Looking for 7th and 8th graders with robotics experience in building, driving, or programming. Team members put those skills to work together on the robotics team. The team meets on Fridays or after school.
items.schedule: Fridays or after school (exact day and time to be confirmed)

items.name: Private Lessons
items.description: Woodward offers private one-on-one musical instruction on campus. Lessons are available for piano and voice, as well as woodwind, brass, percussion, and string instruments. Direct inquiries to stephen.rotz@woodward.edu.

items.name: Debate
items.description: Woodward's nationally competitive Debate Team, the 2021 and 2022 State Champions and 2012 National Champions, is open to all Upper School students taking the Debate class as part of their schedule. Debate sharpens your ability to research and analyze problems, think and listen critically, express thoughts clearly, and better understand public affairs, while building confidence and poise. Tournaments run from September through May, with competition opportunities tailored to each student's needs. Head coaches: Maggie Berthiaume and Becca Steiner.
items.schedule: Tournaments September through May (practice days and times to be confirmed)

items.name: German National Honor Society
items.description: An honor society that recognizes scholarship in German classes. Membership is by invitation only and is based on scholarship in German.

items.name: Upper School Reading Bowl Team
items.description: Team members read the nominees for the Georgia Peach book awards and compete in a Quiz Bowl-style competition against other schools, answering questions about the books.

items.name: Math Team
items.description: The competition math team gives all interested students opportunities to take part in competitive problem solving on campus and around the state. Events include the Kennesaw University Math Competition (round 1 in October and, for qualifiers, round 2 in February), the Rockdale Math Competition in October, the AMC 10/12 A and B tests after school on two days in November, the Westminster Wildcat Math Competition in March, the AIME in March (for qualifiers through AMC 10/12 scores), and the State Math Tournament in April. Dues: $20 for competition entrance fees. Sponsor: Paula Gentry.

items.name: Math Club
items.description: For students who might not think they are good at math, or who lack confidence in it, but still love it. High schoolers from all walks of life are welcome. Members talk about simple proofs to complex problems, properties of numbers, mathematical puzzles and riddles, everyday math, and more, in a non-strenuous environment that does not require a deep understanding of math. Come ready to think outside the box and have fun.

items.name: Model UN
items.description: Students simulate United Nations committees by representing a country whose positions they have researched, taking part in debates and problem-solving negotiations. Members gain a practical understanding of how the UN approaches global issues and reaches decisions. The club typically attends one or more Atlanta-area conferences and one out-of-state travel conference each year, and hosts its own on-campus conference. Any and all interested students in grades 9-12 are welcome. Dues: $20 for conference registrations. Sponsors: Matt Tilford and Linda Wyatt.

items.name: National Honor Society
items.description: Membership is by invitation only and is based on scholarship, leadership, service, and character, with a minimum 3.8 Core GPA. Open to grades 11 and 12 only. See the Scheduling and Curriculum Guide for more detailed information.

items.name: Science Olympiad
items.description: A competitive team of 15 students that competes against other schools in 23 events covering science and engineering fields. The school typically fields three competitive teams. Events include paper-and-pencil knowledge tests, lab activities that demonstrate skill and knowledge, and engineering events where students build a device to be tested at the competition site. The team competes in at least three tournaments each year at the invitational, region, state, and potentially national levels. Dues: $35 for the team jersey and competition registrations. Sponsors: Gary Lawhon, Andrea Patterson, Lesley Carnes, John Faison, and Alex Iakovlev.

items.name: Senior Philosophy Seminar
items.description: A group of about ten seniors, chosen by the sponsors after an application process in the spring. The group meets in the early evening about 8-9 times a year to discuss selected philosophical issues. A textbook, Philosophy: Paradox and Discovery, serves as a guide and is required reading over the summer. Sponsors: Tom Ehrensperger, Chris Lewis, and Jenny Green.
items.schedule: Early evening, about 8-9 times a year (dates to be confirmed)

items.name: Sociedad Honoraria Hispánica
items.description: An honor society for high school students enrolled in Spanish, sponsored by the American Association of Teachers of Spanish and Portuguese (AATSP). Membership is based on scholarship in Spanish classes and is by invitation only. The society hosts several cultural events throughout the year that all Upper School students are invited to attend.

items.name: Société Honoraire de Français
items.description: The National French Honor Society for high school students. Its mission is to stimulate interest in the study of French and Francophone cultures, promote high standards of scholarship, reward scholastic achievement, and foster an inclusive and supportive environment for all learners. Candidates must be in grades 10-12 and enrolled in the fourth semester of French or higher (exceptions can be made for 9th graders with an A average in their last three French courses). Membership is by invitation. Dues: $30, one time, for national charter fees, a certificate, activities, and food at meetings.

items.name: Quill & Scroll
items.description: An international honors society for high school journalists, founded in 1926 at the University of Iowa. It encourages students to pursue careers in journalism and recognizes achievement in journalism and scholastic publication. Woodward has been a Quill and Scroll charter school since October 17, 1977, and recognizes the work of students in The Blade, the butterknife, Silent Voices, and The Phoenix. Membership is by invitation only. Sponsors: Emily Heilker and Kristin Jackson.

items.name: Quiz Bowl Team
items.description: Do you enjoy Jeopardy, High-Q, and trivia games? The team practices regularly during lunch to train for competitions and tournaments throughout the year. Successful members are eligible for award letters and letter jackets. Any student in grades 9-12 with a competitive spirit is welcome, and the team is especially looking for underclassmen who are willing to learn and grow. Coaches: Ian Irwin and Melissa Gilbert. To find out more, contact Mrs. Gilbert in the library.
items.schedule: Regular practices during lunch (days to be confirmed)

items.name: Art Club
items.description: Membership is based on outstanding ability, interest, service, and character, and members must take two semesters of art during the current school year or have been an active member previously. The club inspires and recognizes students dedicated to art and works to bring art to the attention of the Woodward community. Members take part in and sponsor gallery shows and events, and the club organizes or hosts the visiting artists workshop day, museum and gallery visits, Experience the Arts Day, the Art College Visitation Day, and the Senior Art Show and awards presentation. Dues: $15 (includes a T-shirt designed by a member). Sponsors: Andy Cunningham, Jon Grainger, May Engelhart, and Natalie Brandhorst.

items.name: National Art Honor Society
items.description: Provides scholarship opportunities for visual arts students, along with community service projects that pull the community together creatively.

items.name: Coffee House
items.description: An open mic where students perform or read creative work for their peers. In partnership with Silent Voices, it hosts monthly sessions, some in an intimate classroom setting and others in more public venues like the library or the Richardson Amphitheater. Students are invited to take part or just to listen.
items.location: Classrooms, the library, or the Richardson Amphitheater
items.schedule: Monthly sessions (dates to be confirmed)

items.name: Comedy Club
items.description: A place for aspiring actors, writers, comics, and anyone interested in sketch and stand-up comedy to pursue their talents in an accepting and active environment. The club meets once a month to organize comedy performances, take part in community activities, and explore new comedic experiences. Members watch, participate in, and create comedy, and learn skills that are valuable outside the arts. Dues: $20 (T-shirt, end-of-semester party, and comedy event).
items.schedule: Once a month (day and time to be confirmed)

items.name: Thespian Club
items.description: A branch of the International Thespian Society. The club meets once a month to organize theatre outings, service projects, and other group events. In February members attend a weekend State Theatre Conference, and a week-long international conference is available in June. At the conferences, the group attends performances and workshops on acting, singing, mime, dance, lighting, costuming, stage management, and more. Eligibility is based on a point system earned by taking part in the Woodward Theatre Department as an actor, stage manager, designer, or crew member. Dues: $25 (T-shirt, banquets, and food at events and meetings). Sponsors: Erin Greenway, John Brandhorst, and Hannah Barnhart.
items.schedule: Once a month (day and time to be confirmed)

items.name: Thespian Honor Society
items.description: The International Thespian Society (ITS) is the Educational Theatre Association's honorary organization recognizing the achievements of high school theatre students, with troupes chartered in schools across the country. A student can be inducted after earning 10 points, equal to about 100 hours working in school, community, or professional theater, on and backstage. Inducted students can compete at the state convention in Columbus, GA. Induction fee: $10.

items.name: Fall Theatre Production
items.description: The Upper School Theatre Department puts on two productions each fall, one in mid-September and one in mid-October. Students may take part on stage as an actor or behind the scenes by helping with the technical aspects. For more information, contact the theatre director. Technical Director: John Brandhorst. Show fee: $100 (show sweatshirt and meals at evening rehearsals).
items.schedule: Two productions: mid-September and mid-October (rehearsal days and times to be confirmed)

items.name: Spring Musical
items.description: The Theatre Department produces a major musical each February. Auditions are in late November or early December (listed on the school calendar), and each student prepares a song from a Broadway musical and takes part in a dance audition. There are also opportunities to help with the technical production. Technical Director: John Brandhorst. Show fee: $140 (show sweatshirt and meals at evening rehearsals).
items.schedule: Auditions late November or early December; performances in February (rehearsal days and times to be confirmed)

items.name: National Honor Society for Dance Arts
items.description: Celebrates the artistic, academic, and leadership achievements of exceptional dance students. The group promotes a desire for life-long learning in dance, an understanding and appreciation of dance as an art form, and knowledgeable audiences for tomorrow. All dancers in the Woodward Dance program are eligible after one year of participation and 30 earned points.

items.name: Dance Ensemble
items.description: A select group of dancers who perform in the Woodward community, locally and nationally. It is limited to dedicated students with an advanced level of training in ballet, modern, jazz, choreography, and improvisation. Membership is by audition only, with auditions held in the spring. Students receive Honors credit and are eligible for a dance letter jacket after two years of commitment and 40 points. The class meets during school and rehearses after school twice a week for two hours. Directors: Jenny Gould and Charray Helton.
items.schedule: After-school rehearsals twice a week for two hours (days to be confirmed)

items.name: Marching Band
items.description: Known as the Robert W. Woodruff Marching Band, it plays in the stands and at halftime of every football game and marches in parades and competitions in various locales, often earning "Best in Class" awards for music and marching excellence. The music is a mix of fun and pageantry, with the goal of supporting the team and entertaining the home crowd. Open to students in grades 9-12, who benefit from the discipline and hard work of membership. Directors: Jeffrey Rowser and Valerie Morgan.

items.name: Big Band
items.description: A jazz group in the style of the traditional big band: five saxes, four trumpets, four trombones, piano, guitar, bass, drum set, and percussion. The group performs swing classics, rock, and funk at concerts and events throughout the year. This is a year-long membership, mainly for students in the band program, though exceptions can be made.
items.schedule: Tuesdays, after school

items.name: Jazz Band
items.description: A smaller jazz group performing jazz standards with a focus on improvisation, with open instrumentation: horn players, piano, guitar, bass, and drums. The group performs at concerts and events throughout the year. This is a semester membership, mainly for students in the band program, though exceptions can be made.
items.schedule: Rehearsals at designated times (to be confirmed)

items.name: Color Guard / Dance Team
items.description: Performs with the marching band at all football games and select pep rallies, and members are eligible to earn letters. Auditions are held in the spring and are open to all Upper School girls. Dance training and gymnastic ability are not required but are a plus.

items.name: Honors Choral Ensembles
items.description: Membership in the vocal ensembles is by audition only. Camerata Singers is open to 11th and 12th graders, and Jazz Choir is open to grades 9-12. The groups rehearse using a combination of Tuesday evenings and late-start mornings and perform at the choral concerts and in the community. They are featured on Experience the Arts Day, and students earn honors credit for their choir class.
items.schedule: Tuesday evenings and late-start mornings

items.name: WA Cappella
items.description: A male a cappella group that is student led and sponsored by Mr. Rotz. Songs are often pop or other non-classical genres. Participants are members of the choral program. See Mr. Rotz for more information.

items.name: Private Music Lessons
items.description: Woodward offers private one-on-one musical instruction on campus. Lessons are available for piano and voice, as well as woodwind, brass, percussion, and string instruments. Direct inquiries to stephen.rotz@woodward.edu.

items.name: The Blade / the butterknife
items.description: Student-run, advisor-assisted news outlets for the Upper School. The butterknife is a website and weekly newsletter sent to students, staff, and faculty. The Blade is a magazine that publishes longer feature articles twice a semester, including a special Senior Issue at the end of the school year. Students lead all aspects of publishing, with many leadership roles. The staff seeks students interested in writing, photography, graphic design, web design, cartooning, and editing. Membership in the club (or the class) is by application. Contact Mrs. Heilker.

items.name: The Phoenix (Yearbook)
items.description: The Academy-wide yearbook is a project-based, year-long student publications course in journalism. Students interested should demonstrate superior writing and organizational skills. In yearbook, students master interviewing, reporting, writing, graphic design, photography, and time management while meeting the standards of state and national scholastic press associations. Interested students should see Ms. Jackson in Jane Woodruff Hall, room 113.

items.name: Silent Voices Literary Arts Magazine
items.description: Publishes a national award-winning literary arts magazine and web supplement featuring students' creative writing, visual art, films, musical compositions, and choreography. Members gather submissions, then read, view, and curate the best for publication. In the fall students work in InDesign and Photoshop to craft a less formal zine, and in the spring they craft a more formal magazine released around graduation.

items.name: Black Student Union Club
items.description: The Black Student Unity Club (BSU) is a safe space for Black students to discuss pressing or current topics that concern the Black community, and for allies to listen and learn from group discussion. Students are encouraged to express their thoughts and feelings about controversial subjects while being open-minded to others, and members are respected for their opinions. Members also work together on service projects and Black History Month activities, and with the 5 Points Diversity club for broader group discussions. Sponsors: Lorri Hewett and Chelsea Culley-Love.

items.name: Catholic Identity Club
items.description: The club's purpose is simply to support Roman Catholic students at Woodward. Some meetings revolve around theological questions, and others involve community service such as sandwich making for the homeless and making gifts of appreciation for housekeeping staff. A priest or deacon occasionally speaks, usually by Zoom, and the club prays the Rosary every Thursday morning. Sponsors: Jenifer Baro, Jeanne Ann Ratliff, and Tara Ingle.
items.schedule: Rosary every Thursday morning (other meeting times to be confirmed)

items.name: Chinese Club
items.description: Celebrates Chinese language and culture and is open to all Upper School students. Members enjoy cultural activities and festivals such as Lunar New Year, the Mid-Autumn Festival, Chinese calligraphy, paper cutting, Chinese movies, shuttlecock or ping-pong competitions, and dumpling making. Officers and the sponsor organize most events, and members are encouraged to attend and participate. Students pay club dues to become official members. Dues: $20 (food at meetings and activity supplies).

items.name: Fellowship of Christian Athletes
items.description: A Christian organization encouraging athletes to impact the world for Jesus Christ. FCA meets most Tuesdays during lunch in the gym, and lunch is always provided. Meetings feature a guest speaker or student-led talks and discussions to challenge you and help you grow in your faith. Other activities include a spring retreat, weekly Bible study, and volunteer opportunities. Dues: $20 (food at meetings and a T-shirt).
items.schedule: Most Tuesdays, during lunch

items.name: French Club
items.description: Invites all who are interested in French language and culture to join. Members explore the 29 countries that make up the Francophone world beyond France through art, music, and food in a relaxed setting that leaves time to learn and socialize with friends. The club also has a cultural exchange with a school in Haiti and interacts with them over Zoom from time to time. Dues: $5 (food and activity supplies).

items.name: German Club
items.description: German Club is for anyone interested in the German language and culture.

items.name: Genders & Sexualities Alliance
items.description: The GSA offers support to Woodward's LGBT+ population (lesbian, gay, bisexual, transgender, and inclusive of all identities) and educates students and faculty about LGBT+ issues. It acts as a safe zone for LGBT+ students and allies and a place where students of all orientations and genders support one another. An important goal is to make Woodward a more inclusive and understanding place for everyone. Sponsors: Maria Mays, Rachel Norwood, Paul Calvert, and Chelsea Culley-Love.

items.name: Japan Club
items.description: For Japanese language students and any students interested in the language and culture. Dues: $5 (snacks and admission to JapanFest).

items.name: Jewish Student Union
items.description: Builds unity in the Jewish community and educates the larger community about Judaism, for Jewish students and those interested in learning more about Judaism and supporting the Jewish community at Woodward. Activities include meetings with Rabbi Silverman and with Shinshinim (Israeli youth spending a year in Atlanta), a field trip to the Jewish Film Festival, daffodil planting and Holocaust remembrance, and holiday celebrations. Sponsors: Traci Lerner, Chris Lewis, and Jodi Hochman.

items.name: Islamic Awareness Club
items.description: Focuses on the cultural as well as religious aspects of Islam. The club is open to both Muslim and non-Muslim students and explores how Muslim students can celebrate their fondness for America while maintaining their Muslim heritage. Dues: $10 (activity supplies).

items.name: South Asian Affinity Club
items.description: A cultural association for those of South Asian descent that is welcome to all. Members share South Asian culture with the school community through fun, engaging events and foster discussion about issues such as mental health in the South Asian community and other student-selected topics.

items.name: Spanish Club
items.description: Celebrates the Spanish language and the diverse cultures of the Spanish-speaking world. Open to all Upper School students, whether fluent, beginning learners, or not currently enrolled in Spanish. Activities include Día de los Muertos and Hispanic Heritage Month celebrations, learning Latin dances and songs, watching Spanish-language films, tasting traditional foods, and service projects with Spanish-speaking communities. Officers help plan events, and students are encouraged to simply show up and have fun. Dues: $20 (food and snacks at meetings).

items.name: Scouts BSA Troop 631
items.description: A premier leadership and outdoors program for boys (since 1969) and girls (since 2019). Youth leaders decide what the troop does, such as weekend and summer camping, caving, scuba, canoeing, hiking, biking, and other trips, advised by adults. The troop plans to meet most Mondays during the school year at 6 PM, except Mondays after overnight trips, which usually happen about once a month. Girls can be Eagle Scouts too!
items.schedule: Most Mondays during the school year, 6:00 PM

items.name: Interfaith Council
items.description: A leadership group for sharing and exploring religion and spirituality through the Woodward community's diverse experiences and perspectives. All people are welcome in this space. The council meets regularly to plan interfaith conversations, service activities, trips, and other campus-wide events that promote religious literacy and understanding. Speak with Chaplain Chris if you are interested in becoming a part of this group.

items.name: Honor Council & Discipline Board
items.description: Members are selected each spring: Dean Thomas takes nominations from Upper School teachers, and students then vote on the nominated individuals. Advisor: Luke Underwood.

items.name: Honor Guard
items.description: A high-profile group open to Upper School students by invitation and audition. It performs at all home football games, Upper School Convocations, Baccalaureate, graduation ceremonies, and off-campus functions approved by the administration.

items.name: Peer Leadership
items.description: A select group open to juniors and seniors only. Peer leaders work with the ninth grade class to ensure a smooth transition to high school. Applications and tryouts are in the spring. Sponsors: Mark Carrington, Anthony Thomas, Sara Elliot, Nellie Jackson, Swannee Park, Tad Sahara, Chris Myers, and Tonia Webb.

items.name: Athletic Leadership Council
items.description: A group of student athletes who meet regularly with Athletic Department administrators to discuss issues facing today's student athletes and to help improve Woodward athletics through shared ideas and open dialogue. Members also take part in leadership training aligned with the department's PRIDE motto (Perseverance, Respect, Integrity, Determination, and Excellence). Student athletes are invited based on recommendations from varsity head coaches. Meets monthly before school or at lunch. Sponsors: Gene Patterson and Anthony Thomas.
items.schedule: Monthly, before the school day or during lunch (days to be confirmed)

items.name: Big Rocks
items.description: The Big Rocks Student Leadership Committee brings together student leaders from across the Upper School who identify and drive change around high-priority opportunities to strengthen the Woodward Way and create a lasting legacy for future generations. Sponsors: Jen Knox, Andy Cameron, and Darrin Finley.

items.name: Student Admissions Ambassadors
items.description: A select group open to Upper School students by application. Those chosen earn their Woodward requirement of 20 service hours while building leadership skills that strengthen college and scholarship applications. Ambassadors represent the best of Woodward as tour guides and experts on the Woodward education, interacting with prospective families. Applicants must have an open period in their schedule (Study Hall, R Period, or PE) and be excited to share their Woodward experience. Sponsors: Holly Ferguson and Gregory Smith.

items.name: Student Government Association
items.description: Open to all students in grades 9-12. Campaigns and elections for all positions are held in the spring. The SGA functions as a liaison between the student body and the administration. Sponsors: Chris Myers, Chelsea Hagan, Alisha White, Tre Wimby, and Chris Lewis.

items.name: Service Leadership Board
items.description: Makes community service a student-driven initiative. Service Leaders plan, run, advertise, and advocate for service projects, educate peers and younger students about the issues they care about, set the agenda for Woodward Serves club meetings, and connect members to hands-on service. Members must be in 11th or 12th grade and are selected through an application process that begins in early to mid April, with a leadership retreat before school starts in August. Sponsors: Elizabeth Griffin, Laura Campbell, Alexis Horder, Kristin Jackson, Melissa Lawhon, Mo Lotfy, Jacob Snyder, Jon Grainger, and Cortney Stewart.

items.name: Woodward Serves
items.description: WA Serves is Woodward's service club, offering intentional ways to engage in service learning. Monthly club meetings highlight service projects and ways to connect with the community: in the immediate neighborhood (including the Jesse Draper Boys and Girls Club, Horizons Atlanta at Woodward, local elementary schools, Family Life Ministries, and Love Beyond Walls), across Metro Atlanta (including the Atlanta Community Food Bank), and globally with partners around the world. Sponsors: Elizabeth Griffin, Laura Campbell, Alexis Horder, Kristin Jackson, Melissa Lawhon, Mo Lotfy, Jacob Snyder, Jon Grainger, and Cortney Stewart.
items.schedule: Monthly club meetings (day and time to be confirmed)

items.name: Chick-fil-A Leader Academy
items.description: A seven-month leadership and service program sponsored by a local Chick-fil-A restaurant owner. Students start with a service project each fall, take part in monthly "Leader Labs" on vision, values, and servant leadership, complete three service projects, plan a project for "Do Good December," and lead their own Impact Projects in the spring. The program is fully funded through sponsorships, and Operators often serve as business coaches. Sponsors: Dale Stahl and Debra Polk.
items.schedule: Seven-month program with monthly Leader Labs (dates to be confirmed)

items.name: Alternative Investments Club
items.description: Teaches students about markets and how to invest using alternative means such as sneakers, sports cards, or crypto.

items.name: ASL Club (American Sign Language)
items.description: Offers interested students a chance to learn about American Sign Language and Deaf culture. Members learn basic signs for communication and hear from guest visitors who know ASL and Deaf culture.

items.name: Chess & Games Club
items.description: Meets weekly for those interested in competitive or friendly games. All levels are encouraged to join, and the club offers opportunities for tournament play in the Atlanta area.
items.schedule: Weekly (day and time to be confirmed)

items.name: Technology Club
items.description: Explore innovation and invention through hands-on projects that tackle real-world challenges with technology. Members work on coding, electronics, design thinking, prototyping, and 3D printing in a focused yet supportive and casual environment, such as developing an app, building a device to assist people with disabilities, or crafting solutions for environmental sustainability. Students share their work with the broader community, opening doors to entrepreneurial opportunities. Dues: $20.

items.name: Girls Learn International
items.description: A program that empowers and educates middle and high school students to advocate for human rights, gender equality, and access to equitable education. Through a network of student leaders, faculty advisors, parents, and alumni, GLI is building a movement of informed advocates and a new generation of leaders and activists for social change. GLI is for everyone because human rights are for everyone.

items.name: Cooking Club
items.description: For anyone interested in the culinary arts. Throughout the year the club hosts cooking sessions and contests, shares recipes among members, hears from local chefs, and provides food for events around campus. Dues: $20 (food prep supplies).

items.name: DECA Club
items.description: For students interested in marketing, entrepreneurship, finance, hospitality, sports, or leadership, or anyone who wants to become a stronger communicator and decision maker. Members build skills in interviewing, public speaking, problem solving, teamwork, and time management, and compete, collaborate, and make connections. Athletes, leaders, creatives, entrepreneurs, and future business professionals are all welcome, and you do not have to be a business person to belong. Sponsors: Dale Stahl, Debra Polk, and Karen Erwin.

items.name: Dollhouse
items.description: A mentoring and service organization that empowers high school girls through connection, leadership, and community engagement. Members partner with middle school girls as mentors and role models, host guest speakers, take part in service projects, and enjoy activities that strengthen bonds across grade levels. Through mentorship, service, fellowship, and women's empowerment, the club encourages confidence and leadership. Dues: $20 (T-shirt, refreshments, and activity supplies). Sponsors: Monique Williams, Darlene Martin, and Joy Kenyon-Mafu.

items.name: Environmental Awareness Club
items.description: Spreads awareness of the environmental issues facing the campus and student body, for students in grades 9-12 interested in environmental science and community service. Activities include recycling campaigns, guest speakers, and Earth Day activities. Sponsors: Hannah Campbell and Brande Jones.

items.name: Equestrian Team
items.description: The Woodward Hunt Seat IEA equestrian team is open to riders in grades 4 through 12. Interscholastic Equestrian Association riding introduces students to equestrian sports as a team sport, even without owning a horse. Riders compete in classes from Walk/Trot up to Over Fences at 2'6". IEA requires one year of riding experience to participate in shows, and the team is open to riders who can independently walk, trot, and canter, on a space-available basis. Hunt seat show experience is preferred. The team practices weekly at Step-N-Free Stables in Fayetteville, GA, with shows from September through January around Atlanta. Season costs are approximately $2,400 plus a weekly lesson commitment.
items.schedule: Weekly practice (day and time to be confirmed). Shows September through January

items.name: HOSA Club
items.description: HOSA-Future Health Professionals is a student-led organization for students interested in healthcare, medicine, and health-related careers. Members explore different areas of healthcare through educational meetings, guest speakers, service projects, and hands-on activities, and can take part in HOSA's competitive events, which build skills from medical knowledge and health science to leadership and teamwork.

items.name: K-Culture Club
items.description: Formerly the K-pop Appreciation Club, a non-judgmental, inclusive club that celebrates K-pop, K-dramas, K-food, history, language, and Korean culture. Whether you are extremely passionate about Korean culture or new to the K-wave, all are warmly welcomed. Dues: $20 (snacks and food at meetings).

items.name: My Mind Matters Club (M3)
items.description: Open to sophomores, juniors, and seniors, M3 is the student planning committee for the Mental Health Awareness Week events. Weekly or monthly meetings are required to plan the year's events, and an application process takes place in early fall semester. Past events have included therapy dogs, therapeutic painting, a stress-less room, special assembly speakers, and a silent disco. Sponsors: Tonya Dedeaux and Leigh Shelor.

items.name: Outdoors Club
items.description: Open to all students. Members learn skills and take trips such as camping, backpacking, river rafting, skiing, cycling, rock climbing, and other outdoor activities. All trips come with an added cost. Dues: $10 (club stickers, group gear, and trip deposits).

items.name: Paleontology Club
items.description: Educates students about paleontology and archaeology, highlights career opportunities in these fields, and provides hands-on experience through fossil and artifact study, fieldwork simulations, and research projects. No prior experience is required, just curiosity about the natural world and the past. Activities may include guest speakers from local universities and museums, trips to nearby dig sites or collections, and collaborative research on real or replica specimens.

items.name: Pre-Med Club
items.description: Introduces and educates Upper School students about different careers in medicine. Anticipated activities include presentations by medical professionals. Sponsors: Lesley Carnes and Dave Alvord.

items.name: Psychology Club
items.description: Explores the mind, behavior, and mental health through discussions, activities, and projects. Students gain insight into psychology while promoting awareness and wellbeing in the school community. Dues: $8 (snacks at meetings and activity supplies).

items.name: Robotics Club
items.description: Practices 3-4 days a week beginning the second full week of September. The team plans to attend a GRITS or FRC competition in the first semester and, in the second semester, prepares for FIRST competitive matches to qualify for State and hopefully World competition. The team is looking for mechanical and electrical engineers, programmers, and members for outreach, media, mentoring, design, publication, communication, spirit, and scouting. Coaches: Monique Williams, Alex Iakovlev, Brande Jones, and Kelly Lyn.
items.schedule: 3-4 days a week, beginning the second full week of September (days to be confirmed)

items.name: WA Spirit
items.description: Builds enthusiasm and school spirit for athletic, performing arts, and student life events throughout the year. The club meets at least once a month to discuss upcoming events and plan ways to improve student involvement and attendance. Sponsors: Chelsea Hagan, Sara Elliot, and Malia Myers.
items.schedule: At least once a month (day and time to be confirmed)

items.name: UNICEF Club
items.description: A youth-led initiative partnered with UNICEF USA, rooted in the belief that students in the United States have a vital role as the voice for children everywhere. At each monthly meeting, members take part in a service project and watch a documentary about children's issues around the world, and can earn service hours. The club is student led and open to anyone with a passion for helping others and an interest in human rights. Dues: $20 (supplies for service projects).
items.schedule: Monthly meetings (day and time to be confirmed)

items.name: WA Global
items.description: A space for students to gather and share their cultural beliefs and traditions and to learn about groups that may not be directly represented. It builds community among students from diverse backgrounds and welcomes new long-term international students and short-term exchange students as they learn about the culture of Atlanta and Woodward. The club develops a global mindset, global competencies, and global citizenship. Students pursuing the Global Studies Distinction are encouraged to participate. Sponsors: Jaimie Spetseris and Alisha White.

items.name: WA Reads
items.description: Made up of students and teachers who enjoy reading, especially diverse, contemporary young-adult fiction. The club meets once a month during lunch to discuss books read together and individually. All students are encouraged to join the discussions, whether or not they are official members, and the club is committed to fostering a life-long love of reading. Sponsors: Brian Hutcheson and Meredith Zaring.
items.schedule: Once a month, during lunch (day to be confirmed)

items.name: WA Think Tank
items.description: A student-led philosophy and critical-thinking club for anyone curious about the ideas and social forces that shape the world around us. Through open discussions, debates, films, readings, guest speakers, and interactive activities, members explore topics like justice, power, culture, and social change. No prior philosophy experience is needed, just curiosity, respect for different perspectives, and a willingness to question conventional thinking.

items.name: Athletic Team Managers (All Sports)
items.description: Students who want to serve as a team manager for any of the offered sports should contact the head coach about available managing opportunities.

items.name: Cross Country (Boys & Girls)
items.description: Boys and girls varsity cross country. Tryouts begin August 5th at the Willingham Track: bring a watch and a water bottle, and be prepared to run for at least 30 minutes without stopping. Assistant coaches: Pete Fritts, Michael Farry, Leslie Widener, Jimmy Hyder, Isabela Romero, and Sara Elliot.
items.schedule: Fall season; tryouts begin August 5th (practice days and times to be confirmed)

items.name: Football / Gameday Competition Cheerleading
items.description: Tryouts for all squads are held in mid-April for current students, and students who are new to Woodward try out during the first week of summer. Assistant coaches: Elece Lawrence and Jessica Lofton.
items.schedule: Fall season; tryouts in mid-April (practice days and times to be confirmed)

items.name: Football
items.description: Varsity football. Spring practice starts in late April, summer workouts begin the second week of June, and the first official practice is July 22nd. Anyone interested should contact John Hunt. Assistant coaches: Matt Brennan, Ryan Davis, Bill McGarrah, Jason Santana, Lee Sellers, Marquell Beckwith, Ben Grubbs, Erik McMillan, and Glenn Milton.
items.schedule: Fall season; spring practice late April, summer workouts from the 2nd week of June, first official practice July 22nd

items.name: Girls Softball

items.schedule: Tryouts July 29th and 30th

items.name: Riflery
items.description: A co-ed varsity sport for Upper School students (grades 9-12). With adult coaching and supervision, student athletes begin training for the sport of 3 Position, 10 Meter Air Rifle in mid-September and try out for team positions at the end of October. The regular season is November through March, with qualified teams and individuals competing in the postseason in March and April. New or interested students should contact Coach Boenig. Assistant coach: Annie Westlund.
items.schedule: Training begins mid-September; tryouts end of October; season November through March

items.name: Clay Target Team
items.description: Woodward Academy Sporting Clays gives boys and girls in grades 9-12 the chance to take part in trap, skeet, and sporting clays in a supportive environment with trained adult coaches who focus on the safe handling and use of firearms. Tryouts are held in August for all currently enrolled students. New-to-Woodward students can try out in August and should contact Coach Underwood. Assistant coaches: Darren Schneider, Andy Morris, Tonya Whitmire, and Chris Myers.
items.schedule: Tryouts in August

items.description: Varsity boys basketball. Tryouts begin in late October; see one of the coaches to determine which team to try out for. Assistant coaches: Mike Mousadis, Tim Coats, Rob Lawrence, CJ Williams, Mo Lotfy, Julian Cameron, and Tre Wimby.
items.schedule: Winter season; tryouts begin in late October

items.name: Boys & Girls Swimming & Diving
items.description: A no-cut winter sport in the indoor Kennedy Natatorium. The team competes in ten dual meets, four invitationals, a regional meet, and the Georgia State Championships at Georgia Tech. It trains weekdays after school in the water and on land with weights, bands, and other swim-specific workouts, and the season may include an off-campus training trip at an international venue during winter break. The program promotes personal bests and continuous improvement through dedication, discipline, school spirit, and fun. Assistant coaches: Brett Reichert, Kristin Jackson, and Rachel Chou.
items.schedule: Mondays, Tuesdays, Wednesdays, Thursdays, Fridays, after school (winter season)

items.name: Boys Wrestling
